clue.text: Finally help India reassess colonialist history

indicators.note: finally tells us to take the closing letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A call for India to rethink the record of its colonial rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' applies to all four words, not just 'help': their last letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Events gone by are a nation's past, so the word stands as a noun for its history.

clue.text: Following concert, Sue comes back over the moon

indicators.note: following means the remaining letters come after the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: over in the sense of covering, so the reversed name goes round the following word
comes back means the name Sue is read backwards

explanation.surface: After a concert, Sue returns thrilled to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the moon' looks like a phrase for delight, but 'over the' is wordplay: EUS wraps THE to give ETHEUS. Prometheus is a small moon of Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus is a small satellite orbiting Saturn, named after the Titan of Greek myth.

clue.text: Penniless from being part Greek — or by not saving, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
being part says the letters form only part of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man is broke because he is partly Greek or because he never saved.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'from being part' into the definition; 'Penniless' alone is the definition and 'being part' is the hidden signal, with 'from' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no money at all is being utterly broke, so penniless is a synonym.

clue.text: Control station in two stops

parts.note: two with stops asks for two words meaning stop; the first is check, to bring to a halt
the second stop is point, the full stop of punctuation

explanation.surface: A security post placed between two stopping places on a route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two stops' supplies both halves together: CHECK (bring to a halt) and POINT (a full stop); 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkpoint is a barrier where officials control who or what passes, a manned station on a road or border.

clue.text: Worked fast, was winning after cycling thus

indicators.note: after means the winning word follows the cycled letters
cycling means the letters of thus move round, the last coming to the front

parts.note: taken as written before cycling
to have led a race is to have been winning

explanation.surface: Someone pedalled hard and was in front after a bike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bike, but moves the S of THUS to the front: HUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To hustle is to hurry or work energetically, so the past tense means worked quickly.

clue.text: Firms gathering seaweed for fuel

indicators.note: gathering means the firms' letters collect the seaweed inside them

parts.note: COS is the plural of Co, short for company
alga is a seaweed

explanation.surface: Companies harvesting seaweed to make fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal gas was piped to homes for heating and lighting, so it is a fuel.

clue.text: Energy found in seeds from fruit detailed on European symbols of harmony and friendship

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the trimmed fruit sits above the European letter
found in means the energy letter sits inside the seeds

parts.note: pips are fruit seeds
E is the symbol for energy in physics
of means from, as in a man of Kent

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, so the fruit loses its last letter

parts.note: a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: Energy is extracted from seeds of a fruit described at length, alongside some European emblems of goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means cut off at the tail: PEACH becomes PEAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Native American peace pipes were smoked to seal treaties, so they stand for harmony between peoples.

clue.text: Independent satisfied over article

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to have met a demand is to have satisfied it

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper is pleased with a piece it has run.
explanation.definitionFit: An item in a newspaper is a single piece of writing, a news article.

clue.text: Metatarsal's so long

indicators.note: the possessive says the word has the answer within it, in the sense of metatarsal has

explanation.surface: A foot bone of great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like it describes the bone, but it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, as is so long.

clue.text: Zombie, regularly drinking — a bit of Oliver Reed is probably in it

indicators.note: drinking means the regular letters take another letter inside them, as if swallowing it
regularly means taking every other letter of zombie, here the second, fourth and sixth
a bit of means just the opening letter of the name Oliver

explanation.surface: A zombie keeps drinking, and the actor Oliver Reed, a famous hellraiser, is probably involved too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oliver Reed' reads as the boozy actor, but 'Reed' belongs to the definition: a woodwind played through a double reed.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument is sounded through a double reed held in its mouthpiece, so a reed is inside it.

clue.text: Cliff Richard initially invested in Manx getaway, intended to spend advance

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is put inside another, as money is placed in a venture
a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for getaway loses its last letter

parts.note: a getaway is an escape

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the name Richard
to spend means to give up, so the letter for advance is taken out of the word for intended

parts.note: intended means meant
A is used here as a short form of advance, a sum paid ahead

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard puts money into an Isle of Man holiday, meaning to blow his advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff Richard' is the singer, but 'Cliff' alone is the definition. 'Manx' cats are tailless, so the getaway loses its tail; 'to spend' drops A, which stands for advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope or rock face, so it is a type of cliff.

clue.text: Heroic Peston broadcast on two channels

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: The journalist Robert Peston, praised as heroic, is on air across two TV channels.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peston is a well-known British political broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo sound uses two separate audio channels, left and right, to give a sense of space.

clue.text: Devious spy to go legit — perhaps Carter?

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so these letters take a twisted new order

explanation.surface: A crooked spy decides to turn honest.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard Carter was the archaeologist who opened Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922; the question mark shows he is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Carter studied ancient Egypt's remains, making him a specialist in that civilisation, as the definition by example asks.

clue.text: There's important information here concerning a corrupt male on the inside

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: on the inside means the male letter is placed within the word for corrupt

parts.note: to defile is to corrupt or pollute

explanation.surface: A report about a crooked man working as an insider contains vital intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Software ships with a text document of key instructions that users are told to open first.

clue.text: Craftsman's expression of astonishment, wiping bottom and, simultaneously, leg

indicators.note: wiping bottom means the last letter is removed, the bottom of a down entry

parts.note: stone me is a British exclamation of surprise
as means while, at the same time
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A craftsman exclaims in surprise while cleaning a backside and a leg at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiping bottom' looks like a bathroom chore but drops the final E of STONE ME, a British exclamation. In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses stone, a craftsman.

clue.text: Personnel concealing anger for employer

indicators.note: concealing means the personnel letters wrap round and hide the word for anger

parts.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department
ire is anger

explanation.surface: The HR department is hiding its fury at the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hires a person or thing engages them for work or use, an employer in the broad sense.

clue.text: Antagonise cult, capturing a very strong princess first

indicators.note: first means the princess's letters come before everything else

parts.note: Di, Princess Diana, is the usual crossword princess

indicators.note: capturing means the word for cult holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cult is a sect
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud or strong

explanation.surface: A cult upsets people by taking a formidable princess prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very strong' looks like praise of the princess but is the musical marking fortissimo; 'capturing' makes SAFFECT, and 'first' puts the princess before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disaffect people is to turn them against something, to make them hostile or alienated.

clue.text: Trendy name for a pub

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Choosing a fashionable name for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a tavern or public house, a place selling drinks and often lodging.

clue.text: Ignorant hunk, now in gardening trousers

indicators.note: trousers is a verb here, to pocket or take in, so these words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A hunky gardener in his work trousers is clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets, signalling letters held inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware or lacking knowledge is being ignorant; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Bill's arrived with agency

parts.note: in means arrived, as a train that is in
voice means agency, a say or means of acting

explanation.surface: A bill has come in from an agency.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a statement of money owed for goods or services, which is a bill.

clue.text: For example, Hoover's sweeping

definitions.meaning: Hoover is a brand name that became the everyday word for any vacuum cleaner, a trade name used for the whole class

explanation.surface: Using a vacuum cleaner, as an example of cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweeping' looks like housework alongside the Hoover, but means broad. In Britain 'hoover' is the common word for any vacuum cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand name used for every product of its type is a broad, non-specific term, and sweeping statements are broad ones.

clue.text: Space Professor's way of putting things

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, the width of the letter N
a don is a university teacher or professor

explanation.surface: A space scientist's characteristic manner of expressing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space Professor' reads like an astronomer, but it is two pieces; 'way of putting things' means a way of placing objects, not of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing objects end to end, ends touching, is a particular arrangement, a manner of positioning them.

clue.text: Harry, Meghan and Vicar have a little stress at the start — some people take it on the chin

definitions.text: some people take it on the chin

indicators.note: at the start places that letter at the very beginning
a little of the word stress means just its first letter
to harry is to harass or disturb, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Prince Harry, Meghan and a clergyman feel a bit of strain at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince alongside Meghan, but it is the anagram signal for MEGHAN and VICAR; S comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam smeared over the jaw before a razor is used is lather applied to the chin, a playful twist on the idiom.

clue.text: This will make 26 sound like fiction

definitions.text: This will make 26 sound like fiction

parts.words: This will make 26 sound like fiction
parts.note: a speech impediment turning s into th makes the word for girl at 26 come out as myth, a fiction

explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is MISS; said with this impediment it becomes 'mith', that is MYTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech defect pronouncing s as th is exactly what changes the girl's title into myth.

clue.text: Spots a knight in church

indicators.note: in means the knight's letter is placed inside the church's

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone notices a knight inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb, noticing, but is a plural noun for pimples.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so spots is the everyday word for it.

clue.text: Explosive journal on Van Gogh discovered

indicators.note: on means the journal word comes after, attached to the trimmed name
discovered means uncovered, so the name loses its outer letters

parts.note: Vincent was Van Gogh's first name
a journal is a diary

explanation.surface: A shocking diary about the painter Van Gogh has come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like 'found' but means stripped of its cover: VINCENT loses V and T to leave INCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An incendiary device is a fire bomb, and the word also means inflammatory, so explosive fits both senses.

clue.text: Pine for a girl

definitions.meaning: to pine for something is to long for it, to feel its absence
a young unmarried woman, addressed by title

explanation.surface: Longing for a particular young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is to regret an absence, the other is the title for an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Foresight of Trump's running mate defining Republican key initiative at the start

indicators.note: defining in the sense of marking the bounds of, so the running mate's name encloses the other letters

parts.note: Mike Pence was Donald Trump's vice-presidential running mate
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: at the start means only the first letter of initiative

explanation.surface: Mike Pence shows foresight by setting out a key Republican initiative at the outset of a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defining' signals containment, the running mate's name bounding the other letters; Mike Pence was Trump's vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowing things before they happen, which is foresight; the two nouns are near synonyms.

clue.text: Heard any gas

parts.note: the word any said aloud sounds like the letter names en and ee, which make NE, the chemical symbol for this noble gas

explanation.surface: Asking whether anyone has smelt a gas leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The sounded letters give only the element's symbol, so the clue works as a cryptic definition: the symbol stands for the whole element.
explanation.definitionFit: The element with symbol Ne is a noble gas used in glowing signs, so it is a gas.
